prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept / illustration-story. Create ONE exceptional, finished portrait CARD BACK for COSYWORLD, a whimsical cosmic-horror storybook card game. Aspect ratio 2:3, high resolution, full-bleed opaque artwork. The card back itself is the closed lid of an INTRICATELY CARVED WOODEN BOX, viewed precisely straight down, parallel to the picture plane. The rectangular heirloom box lid fills essentially the entire image; its own softened rounded wooden edges form the card perimeter. This is usable flat card-back artwork, no presentation mockup, surrounding tabletop, hands, lettering, logos, extra cards or perspective tilt.

Research-grounded creative direction: Cosyworld's named Intricately Carved Wooden Box has an old narrative association with a mysterious glowing orb and a choice to encounter the unknown. The current game's art is richly hand-painted ink and gouache/watercolor, worn wood and brass, warm amber light, blue-black and indigo shadow, domestic comfort with subtle cosmic strangeness. Its places include a mirror attic, black pond, warm cottage embraced by trees, and a willow-lined river; its familiar objects include an oil lamp, a worn bell and wooden buttons, and its cast includes Pip the moth. The creator's dreaming-oak premise uses the same forms across scales: branches become paths and rivers; tree rings become ponds, mirrors and dream openings. Translate that identity into an original crafted object. The image must feel physically touchable, intimate, kept and quietly mysterious.

Composition and carving: a broad double-beveled rounded-rectangle rim encloses a fitted raised lid, with a precise narrow dark seam between lid and shallow case and tiny antique-brass corner fastenings. Deep, intricate but cleanly organized relief carving in aged oak and dark walnut. Two great intertwining oak boughs and their roots form a balanced wreath around a central circular medallion. Roots curl into nested rings and branch again into smaller branches; real oak leaves, acorns and slender willow leaves are sculpted into the wood, with convincing undercuts and individually readable chisel facets. In the top and bottom ornament, hide one paired moth-wing shape each, rotated counterparts and made from the very same carved wood, not separate insects. Two small opposing bell-like shapes are subtly discovered in the side scrollwork, subordinate to the organic carving. Carving should feel like patient human craftsmanship, not a random tangle or generic printed filigree.

Focal point: a beautifully carved roundel of concentric oak-growth rings at the exact center, about one third of the lid width. At its center, a small polished nearly-black moonstone or dark glass inset held by carved wood, about one seventh of the card width. Its deep still surface and a few restrained pale amber and star-mint pinpoints suggest an immense hidden depth. A very thin, barely escaping amber light in part of the fitted lid seam implies something alive and luminous still enclosed inside the closed box. Keep this supernatural accent subtle. The wooden box remains the subject, with over ninety percent of the image visually wood and carving. No exposed glowing sphere, no open lid, no eye, no faces.

Card-back discipline: clear large nested shapes that read at 150-pixel width, exquisite secondary details visible on close inspection; main carved pattern has 180-degree rotational symmetry and feels equally intentional upside down. Opposing paired motifs, no upright scenic illustration or obvious top. A calm central focus amid dense perimeter relief. Strong inset border, generous structural frame, protected ornament at the corners. Very slight handmade irregularity and natural grain should preserve the realism of the object.

Materials, color and finish: rich medium brown and deep walnut, rubbed honey-colored edges, visible flowing wood grain, shallow dents from years of handling, dust in the deepest cuts, muted old brass and a few restrained moss-dark patina notes. Warm lamplight softly grazes the carved facets, with cool indigo-charcoal in the deep recesses; the entire pattern stays legible, do not crush it into darkness. Painted tactile realism with fine ink contours, matte gouache pigment and hand-painted watercolor nuance, the material detail and inviting glow of an exquisitely illustrated old storybook. Depth comes from carved relief and delicately painted light, not glossy CGI or metallic gilding. Avoid ornamental excess that obscures the box, gold-plated tarot aesthetics, runes, writing, text, numerals, skulls, weapons, glowing neon, flat vector ornament, cartoon plastic, photographic mockup and external scenery. A whole strange world could be carefully put away in this small wooden box.
